claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories for publishing packages per the strategies in this guide (one package per repository, cohesive components).
Pulumi packages come in two flavors (source-based and executable-based), and each is versioned and released differently.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and the package's version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow, typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
Publishing a source-based package to the Private Registry involves applying a semver Git tag (e.g., v1.2.3) to the repository.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
The `pulumi package publish` step often runs automated tests before publishing.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Executable-based package releases are produced by a CI/CD pipeline that builds the plugin, generates the SDKs, and pushes everything to the relevant feeds.
In both source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights the way Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and expected, and the components ship together at the package's version.
Pulumi recommends defining exactly one package per repository, grouping a cohesive set of components in that package, and using multiple repositories (one per package) for distinct packages.

The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry (at pulumi.com/registry/packages/eks/) bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with the supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
A single `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repository root defines a package, with components living alongside it.
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way, regardless of whether each component changed.
The Pulumi IDP Private Registry concept page exists at /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/.
The CLI reference page for `pulumi package publish` exists at /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/.
A Publishing packages guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.
The packaging-components guide has anchors for source-based-plugin-packages and executable-based-plugin-packages.
